answer: A place in my hometown that I have always loved is the old square in the centre of Sirajganj, which is really the heart of the town. It sits at a busy crossroads not far from the main bazaar, and almost every rickshaw in town seems to pass through it at some point. It has been there for generations, and it holds a lot of [[nostalgia]] for me. As a child I would play there, and even now I find myself [[drawn back to]] it most weekends. My father used to take me there on the back of his bicycle to buy sweets, and I still go to the same sweet shop today. The square is surrounded by old shops, some with faded signboards that must be decades old, giving it a wonderfully [[quaint]] character. In the evenings it comes alive, with families strolling, vendors selling snacks and friends gathering to chat. I usually meet a couple of old school friends there, and we sit at a tea stall and talk about cricket or work for an hour or so. What I love most is that it has remained largely unchanged over the years, which is comforting in a fast-moving world. It feels like a place where the whole community naturally comes together, whatever their age or background. Honestly, being there always fills me with a warm sense of [[belonging]]. It is a simple place, but it means a great deal to me and to everyone who grew up there, and I hope it is never [[torn down]] in the name of development.

followUps.q: Has the square changed much since you were a child?
followUps.answer: A little. Some of the old shops have been replaced by mobile phone shops, and there is more traffic now. But the basic layout and the evening atmosphere are exactly as I remember them.

followUps.q: Would you take a visitor there?
followUps.answer: Yes, definitely. If someone wanted to understand everyday life in Sirajganj, I would take them there in the evening, buy them some sweets and just let them watch the town go by.
